subject: ScoutAI - post-call deployment readiness & SLOs
messages:
From: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.ai>
To: Liam Carter <liam@scoutai.com>, Priya Shah <priya.shah@scoutai.com>
Cc: Jasmine Liu <jasmine@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 28 Oct 2026 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: ScoutAI — post-call summary, priorities & next steps

Hi Liam / Priya — thanks again for the deep dive earlier. Quick recap and the actions we discussed so your team has a single place to reference. Happy to hop on another short call if anything looks off.

Key pain points you shared:
- Prediction latency spikes during peak trading windows (affects real-time suggestion UX).
- Holding costs from wasted GPU cycles on repeated context windows.
- Security/regulatory requirement: model hosting must be in a customer-dedicated VPC; audit trail for inference logs for 12 months.

Goals from the call:
- Replace current on-prem prototype with a predictable-hosted or dedicated deployment that keeps p95 latency <= 120ms for short prompts (<=128 tokens) and p95 <= 450ms for longer, multi-turn flows (<=1024 tokens).
- Support sustained steady-state throughput of ~120 QPS for the primary endpoint, with bursting to 350 QPS for short periods.
- Keep token cost comparable to current infra; prefer caching/batching over always-upgrading GPU size.

Technical summary we sketched:
- Model: Llama-3 70B (quantized int8 or awq), with a warm KV-cache for frequent prefixes.
- Topology: Dedicated GPU pool (multi-AZ) with single-region primary (us-west2) and failover to us-east1; traffic split by latency and cost policy.
- Autoscaling: target CPU/GPU utilization based autoscale with burst capacity; predictable reserve for trading hours.
- Fallbacks: smaller 13B variant for low-cost fallback in degradations.
- Security: private VPC peering, customer-managed KMS, and 12m audit retention.

Immediate next steps (owners):
- Aditya/RD: provide a deployment sketch + rough cost delta using dedicated pool + caching by EOD Thu (attachment: initial topology png). (Owner: Aditya)
- ScoutAI: share a short representative prompt set + 72h traffic pattern (Owner: Priya)
- Jasmine: run quick perf estimate for Llama-3 70B int8 with KV-cache assumptions and share sizing guidance. (Owner: Jasmine)

Attachments: scout_mvp_requirements.pdf (your spec), redwood-deploy-topology.png (sketch we discussed).

Thanks — will follow up with the sizing note in the morning.

Best,
Aditya Rao
Enterprise Solutions
Redwood Inference
---

Thanks Aditya — that captures it well. A couple of clarifications from our side:

Priya Shah

From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine@redwood.ai>
To: Priya Shah <priya.shah@scoutai.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.ai>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 29 Oct 2026 07:25:00 -0700
Subject: RE: ScoutAI — perf sizing assumptions (initial)

Good morning — I ran a quick back-of-envelope perf estimate based on the prompt set you described on the call and our standard quantized 70B profile. Summaries below; I’ll follow with a short spreadsheet.

Assumptions:
- Model: Llama-3 70B (AWQ int8-ish)
- Average prompt length (suggestions): 90 tokens; bursts up to 900 tokens on complex flows
- KV-cache hit-rate target: 42% for suggestions (based on prefix reuse you mentioned)

Sizing (starting point):
- Dedicated pool: 6x A100s (40GB) with continuous batching tuned to 30ms batching delay for low-latency traffic; expected steady-state throughput ~110–140 QPS for short prompts with p95 latency 80–140ms; can burst to ~360 QPS for short windows when we scale to 9x GPUs.
- If you require p95 <= 120ms consistently at steady-state, plan to start with 8x A100s and reserve burst to 12x.
- Cost levers: aggressive KV-cache (prefix caching) reduces token compute by ~30% for suggestion flows; rerouting cold traffic to 13B fallback reduces cost by another ~20% but increases p95 for those flows to 300–500ms.

Operational notes:
- Canary plan: start with 5% traffic on dedicated pool, safety timeout at 500ms, automatic fallback to 13B on policy breach.
- Monitoring: per-route p95/p50, per-model token counts, cache-hit metrics; set an alert if cache-hit drops >15% dur.

Next steps I’ll take today:
- Create sizing spreadsheet + cost delta (Aditya to review before sending to Scout).
- Draft the audit-log schema we produce for inference (fields + retention) and send to Priya.

-Jasmine
Senior Solutions Architect
Redwood Inference
